nodes.label: assertExoIntactRawTextBoundary
nodes.doc: Raw text has NO escape mechanism, so escaping cannot hold the boundary: a static carrying the closing sequence ends the element where it stands.

nodes.label: assertExoNoElementInRawText
nodes.doc: Inside a raw-text or RCDATA element everything up to the closing sequence is characters, so no markup a server prints will be parsed back into an element.

nodes.label: assertExoNoTextAfterChildrenPort
nodes.doc: A region is anchored on the NEXT STATIC ELEMENT, so static text after a children port lands before the rows on the server and after them in the browser.

nodes.label: assertExoNoTextPortInRawText
nodes.doc: The HTML serialiser does not escape a Text node whose parent is one of these, so the server's escaped bytes reach the script's source as `<` — and writing it raw instead is a server-only injection, because nothing escapes `</script`.

nodes.label: assertExoParserStableText
nodes.doc: A run of static text is foster-parented out of a table the same way an element is, and a run that is only whitespace is not.

nodes.label: assertExoServablePropertyPort
nodes.doc: Both compilers cut the markup exactly ONCE per port, in numbering order, so this port's writer can only emit bytes at its own slot — reaching the `<option>`s from a `<select>`'s open tag is a change to the wire format, not a fix to a write…

nodes.label: assertExoSoleChildRawTextPort

nodes.label: assertExoUniqueAttr
